question.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(x)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(x)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+3x-10}{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-9x+18}=0.
$$

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}+3x-10}{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-9x+18} \\  & =\frac{(x+5)(x-2)}{{x}^{2}(x-2)-9(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{(x+5)(x-2)}{({x}^{2}-9)(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{(x+5)(x-2)}{(x+3)(x-3)(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{(x+5)\cancel{(x-2)}}{(x+3)(x-3)\cancel{(x-2)}} \\  & =\frac{(x+5)}{(x+3)(x-3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5=0\,⟹\,x=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to $f(x)=0$ is $x=-5.$
